reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: Al additions are known to promote B2 ordering in refractory high-entropy alloys, and coherent nano-precipitates can effectively strengthen at high temperatures via Orowan bypass, though the specific 3 at% Al and predicted 30–50% strength increase are somewhat speculative without prior data in this exact system.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification experiment is clear and feasible, with specific measurements (TEM/APT, high-temperature mechanical tests) and a quantitative criterion (≥25% yield strength increase), though the exact aging treatment and Al content may require optimization.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses the core problem of high-temperature strength loss with a well-defined, testable intervention and mechanism, making it directly useful for researchers working on this alloy system.
